lines.trans: I noticed Go Yang-mi did not come into work today?
They say she is sick.
How could a woman tough enough to play cat's cradle with steel wire ever get sick? Is she not faking it?
Come to think of it, this is the very first time she has missed work since I joined KBS.
Excuse me, I would like to take a pack of copy paper.
Wait a minute—are you really allowed to hand out multiple packs just like that?
Even so, if you hand out stacks to everyone who asks, Ms. Go Yang-mi will literally faint if she finds out!
Does she know this is happening or not—when is she coming back?!

meanings.note: Used as promissive polite (가져갈게요.).

examples.text: 이거 유출되면 안 되니까 일단 내가 가져갈게요.
examples.trans: Since this photo must never leak out, I will take the memory card with me for now.
Let us do that (will take it along) right away.

meanings.note: Used as noun + instrumental (강철로).

examples.text: 무슨 강철로 실뜨기하게 생긴 여자가 아프긴 아파? 뻥 아니야?
examples.trans: How could a woman tough enough to play cat's cradle with steel wire ever get sick? Is she not faking it?
This point about with steel wire is really important.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used as past adnominal (결근한).

examples.text: 그러고 보니까 나 입사하고 처음이다, 그 여자 결근한 거.
examples.trans: Come to think of it, this is the very first time she has missed work since I joined KBS.
Let us do that (was absent from work) right away.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Used as idiom prospective adnominal (기절초풍할).

examples.text: 그래도요, 달란다고 이렇게 막 다 줘버리면 고양미 씨가 알면 진짜 기절초풍할 일인데!
examples.trans: Even so, if you hand out stacks to everyone who asks, Ms. Go Yang-mi will literally faint if she finds out!
Let us do that (faint dead away) right away.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)
meanings.note: Used for ratings, test scores, or results coming out

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 나는 단 거 싫어하니까 시럽을 아예 넣지 말라 그랬지!
examples.trans: I hate sweet drinks, so I told you not to put any syrup in at all!
This expression comes from 'sweet'.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: used in 막을 내리다 / 막 내리다 ('to bring down the curtain', i.e., to end a show or era)

examples.trans: The performance came to an end.
The stage curtain went up.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Used as slang noun (뻥).

examples.text: 무슨 강철로 실뜨기하게 생긴 여자가 아프긴 아파? 뻥 아니야?
examples.trans: How could a woman tough enough to play cat's cradle with steel wire ever get sick? Is she not faking it?
This point about a fib, bluff is really important.

meanings.note: Used as resultative -게 (실뜨기하게).

examples.text: 무슨 강철로 실뜨기하게 생긴 여자가 아프긴 아파? 뻥 아니야?
examples.trans: How could a woman tough enough to play cat's cradle with steel wire ever get sick? Is she not faking it?
Let us do that (play cat's cradle) right away.
Did you hear about this Ms.?
I was busy today because of Ms..

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

examples.text: 이거 들어 드리려고요. 예진 선배님 손목 다쳐서 아픕니다.
examples.trans: To carry these for her. Senior Ye-jin hurt her wrist and is in pain.
Today's atmosphere is truly hurts, is in pain.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for location.

examples.trans: Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?

meanings.note: interrogative noun asking about time; combines with particles like -부터 (from)

examples.trans: When did you come to Korea?
Since when have you worked here?
Did you hear about this female?
I was busy today because of female.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken contraction of 이것.

examples.trans: How much is this?
Please look at this.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral used with counters and in numbers

examples.trans: Let's meet in the first-floor lobby.

examples.text: 일 호선이 가장 오래된 지하철 노선이에요.
examples.trans: Line 1 is the oldest subway line.

meanings.note: Used as connective -고 (입사하고).

examples.text: 사실 입사하고 처음으로 회사가 참 좋은 곳이구나 이런 생각이 들었습니다.
examples.trans: Honestly, for the first time since joining KBS, I thought: what a wonderful workplace this is!
Let us do that (joining the company and) right away.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Used as hesitation interjection (저기).

examples.text: 아니 저기 백승찬, 너 뭐 하니? 나 지금 좀 당황스러우려고 그런다.
examples.trans: Wait, Baek Seung-chan, what are you doing? You are starting to fluster me right now.
Please pull over at the taxi stand over there.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 너네 팀이 종이 타러 가면 행정반에서 별소리 안 하고 주지?
examples.trans: When your team goes to pick up paper, the admin desk hands it over without a fuss, right?
Here the word for 'paper' is key.

meanings.note: Used as conditional -면 (줘버리면).

examples.text: 그래도요, 달란다고 이렇게 막 다 줘버리면 고양미 씨가 알면 진짜 기절초풍할 일인데!
examples.trans: Even so, if you hand out stacks to everyone who asks, Ms. Go Yang-mi will literally faint if she finds out!

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

meanings.note: 처음부터 means 'from the start'

examples.trans: Let's start over from the beginning.
This is my first time coming to Seoul.
